answer: An agent market serving an orchard, a basalt quarry, or a sparrow survey can require every active identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days. A proven instance of double billing burns that identity’s bond. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000, and using them to submit fraudulent bills risks losing it. New names cannot bypass the bond, so identities remain cheap to invent but costly to operate at scale.
